newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SOCCER-VIALLI SHINES FOR CHELSEA ON 'CHILL OUT' TOUR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VIALLI SHINES FOR CHELSEA ON 'CHILL OUT' TOUR.

text.p: HONG KONG, May 20, Reuter - Italy's Gianluca Vialli, who came on for only two minutes at the end of Chelsea's F.A. Cup final victory at Wembley last week, scored two goals on Tuesday in his side's 3-2 friendly win over Hong Kong's South China side.

It was literally and metaphorically thousands of miles away from Wembley Stadium, but 10,500 fans in the compact Siu Sai Wan sports enjoyed a good show, one month before the British flag is lowered on the colony and China takes over.

Captain Dennis Wise and Mark Hughes were missing from the Cup final but Vialli, who spent most of Saturday afternoon on the bench, scored in the 37th and 40th minutes to demonstrate he is not a spent force.
Italian midfielder Roberto Di Matteo, who scored the fastest ever Wembley Cup final goal in 43 seconds on Saturday, added a third just before halftime.
Di Matteo and compatriot Gianfranco Zola, England's Footballer of the Year, then went off.

Chelsea stroked the ball about in the high humidity in the second half until they were given a bit of a shock by South China who scored through Shum Kwok-pui in the 71st minute and Ricky Cheng with the last kick of the ball.

"We are pretty pleased to be out here as the atmosphere back home was not right for a holiday," said Chelsea's Dutch manager Ruud Gullit. "This gives us the chance to experience Asian football and chill out."

When England played in Hong Kong a year ago Paul Gascoigne and several team mates hit the headlines for wild partying in The Jump nightclub and Gullit was asked if his players would be allowed to go out on the town and try the infamous "dentist's chair" where drinks are poured down patrons' throats from bottles of spirits.
"As long as there are no journalists around," Gullit replied.
